title: Balanced Haloumi and Mixed Grain Salad
subtitle: with Sweet Leek Dressing
description: Our 'balanced' recipes are just that – high in nutritive value (that's fibre-rich veggies, lean proteins and wholegrains, just between us), so these dishes are good for you in every which way! They're perfect for anyone looking to minimise their intake of refined foods without sacrificing on taste.

ingredients.name: Brown and Black Rice with Quinoa

steps.text: Cook rice blend: Preheat the oven to 220C, fan-forced. Line an oven tray with baking paper. Fill a medium saucepan three-quarters full with water and bring to the boil. Add the rice blend and cook for 22-24 mins until tender. Drain.

Prep ingredients: Meanwhile, cut the unpeeled pumpkin into 1cm-thick wedges (see Kitchen 101). Halve the leek lengthwise and thinly slice the pale stem, discarding any dark green stem. Crush 1 garlic clove. Thinly slice the haloumi. Pick the mint leaves, discarding the stems.

Roast pumpkin: Put the pumpkin on the lined tray, drizzle with 2 tsp olive oil, season with salt and pepper and toss to coat. Roast for 20 mins or until golden and tender. Meanwhile, put the garlic, 1 tbs white wine vinegar and 1 tsp dijon mustard in a large bowl. Season with salt and pepper and whisk to combine.

Soften leek: Heat 2 tsp olive oil in a medium frypan over medium heat. Cook the leek, stirring occasionally, for 5 mins or until softened. Add the currants, 2 tsp white wine vinegar, 1 tsp honey and 1 tbs water and season with salt and pepper. Cook for a further 2 mins or until slightly caramelised. Remove from the pan and wipe the pan clean.

Fry haloumi and serve up: Heat 2 tsp olive oil in the same pan over medium-high heat. Cook the haloumi for 1-2 mins each side until golden. Remove the pan from the heat. Add the rice blend and leek mixture to the dressing and toss to combine. Divide the grain salad, pumpkin and haloumi among plates. Scatter over the mint leaves and enjoy!
Kitchen 101: Pumpkin skin is edible, nutritious and delicious, especially when roasted. Leaving it on also saves time and waste, but you can remove it if you prefer.
